evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Character Database)
evidence.field: 形義通解; competing graphic-origin analyses
evidence.text: The entry says oracle, bronze, and seal constructions are the same and that the original meaning is unknown. It records Xu Shen’s heaven-and-earth interpretation and Zhu Fangpu’s agreement, alongside proposals that the graph was a tally mark (Yu Shengwu), an early form of 互 depicting a cord-gathering device (Ding Shan), or an outstretched hand/palm lines (Zhang Bingquan). The entry reports Ji Xusheng’s objection that a five-horizontal-stroke form was 四 with a decorative stroke, not 五. These are attributed analyses; the page does not establish a pre-numeral sense or the name and pronunciation of the proposed cord device.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：漢字甲骨部件分析

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Character Database)
evidence.text: The entry cites 合集 14316, where 五 counts dogs and sheep in a sacrificial offering, and 合集 6 for 五月. These attest cardinal and ordinal uses in the oracle-bone corpus. The entry does not date these specific inscriptions to a reign or calendar year.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：漢字甲骨部件分析

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Character Database)
evidence.field: 金文用例; 戰國竹簡用例; 秦簡 and 帛書通假用例
evidence.text: The entry gives bronze examples of numeral 五, including 尹姞鬲「易玉五品」 and 五年師…𣪕, and Warring States bamboo-slip examples as a numeral and place name. It also reports later manuscript readings of the graph as 伍 in Qin slips, 語 in a Qin daybook, and 吾 in a Mawangdui Laozi manuscript. These are separate reported uses; the entry does not establish a complete semantic chronology or a bridge from a proposed original pictorial referent to the numeral.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：漢字甲骨部件分析

evidence.source: 中國哲學書電子化計劃 (Chinese Text Project)
evidence.text: The Shuowen entry reads 五，五行也。从二，陰陽在天地閒交午也。凡五之屬皆从五. This records Xu Shen’s Han-era account connecting the graph with the Five Phases and the crossing of yin and yang between heaven and earth; it is evidence for his interpretation, not independent proof of graphic origin.
evidence.title: 說文解字 : 卷十五 : 五部

Inspected exact Commons description pages, including labels, provenance and reuse terms. Clicked both original-file links; web fetches failed with cache miss, but the exact direct image URLs were supplied by those pages.

gaps: The graph’s original motivation remains unresolved. The consulted paleographic entry reports competing analyses rather than a settled account; no component-by-component semantic or phonetic analysis applies to 五 in these sources.
The proposed cord-device analysis lacks independently established object name and pronunciation, so no sound-based borrowing account can be verified from it.

The inspected evidence attests numeral and ordinal use in oracle-bone examples but does not establish the first use of the graph or a prior non-numeral stage. The CUHK page does not provide specific calendar dating for its cited examples.
Later manuscript uses as 伍, 語, and 吾 are reported by CUHK, but their earliest occurrences and full borrowing history were not traced.
The Unicode Unihan page was attempted but returned an internal fetch error; the supplied dossier’s reading metadata was not independently verified in this run.

No inscription image or glyph pixels were visually inspected. The two Commons candidates are modern redraws; their direct-image fetches failed, though their exact URLs and source-page provenance were verified.
